columns.mass_kg: Mass of the engine, animal or object, kg.

columns.power_high_w: Highest known power of the class.
columns.power_example_w: Power of the marked example object.
columns.power_max_w: Maximum allowable power; empty if none.

rows.name: Human brain
rows.citation: Raichle M.E. & Gusnard D.A. (2002) Appraising the brain's energy budget. PNAS 99, 10237
rows.notes: About 20 W: a fifth of resting metabolism

rows.name: Horse
rows.citation: Stevenson R.D. & Wassersug R.J. (1993) Horsepower from a horse. Nature 364, 195
rows.notes: Peak 14.9 hp measured; 1 hp = 746 W is a sustained rate; mass approximate

rows.name: Saturn V F-1 rocket engine
rows.citation: Bilstein R.E. (1980) Stages to Saturn: a technological history of the Apollo/Saturn launch vehicles. NASA SP-4206
rows.notes: Jet power = thrust x exhaust speed / 2 with 6.77 MN and Isp 263 s

rows.name: Saturn V at liftoff
rows.citation: Bilstein R.E. (1980) Stages to Saturn: a technological history of the Apollo/Saturn launch vehicles. NASA SP-4206

rows.name: Sun
rows.citation: Williams D.R., NASA Sun Fact Sheet, NSSDCA (2024)
rows.notes: Cap is the Eddington luminosity for one solar mass

rows.name: Quasar J0529-4351
rows.citation: Wolf C. et al. (2024) The accretion of a solar mass per day by a 17-billion solar mass black hole. Nature Astronomy 8, 520
rows.notes: Most luminous known quasar: close to its Eddington limit

rows.name: GW150914 merger (peak)
rows.citation: Abbott B.P. et al. (2016) Observation of gravitational waves from a binary black hole merger. PRL 116, 061102
rows.notes: Peak gravitational-wave luminosity 3.6e49 W: 1/1000 of c^5/G

rows.name: Human body at rest
rows.citation: Henry C.J.K. (2005) Basal metabolic rate studies in humans: measurement and development of new equations. Public Health Nutr 8, 1133
rows.notes: About 1700 kcal per day for a 70 kg adult (approximate)

rows.name: World-class track cyclist (peak)
rows.citation: Dorel S. et al. (2005) Torque and power-velocity relationships in cycling: relevance to track sprint performance in world-class cyclists. Int J Sports Med 26, 739
rows.notes: Pmax 1600 +/- 116 W for a few seconds; body mass approximate

rows.name: Earth's internal heat flow
rows.citation: Davies J.H. & Davies D.R. (2010) Earth's surface heat flux. Solid Earth 1, 5
rows.notes: 47 TW leaks out through the crust: radioactivity plus primordial heat

rows.name: Jupiter's internal heat
rows.citation: Li L. et al. (2018) Less absorbed solar energy and more internal heat for Jupiter. Nat Commun 9, 3709
rows.notes: 7.485 W/m2 over the whole planet (computed): Jupiter is still cooling from its formation

rows.name: Crab pulsar spin-down
rows.citation: Hester J.J. (2008) The Crab Nebula: an astrophysical chimera. ARA&A 46, 127
rows.notes: 5e38 erg/s drawn from the neutron star's rotation powers the whole nebula

rows.name: R136a1 (most massive known star)
rows.citation: Crowther P.A. et al. (2010) The R136 star cluster hosts several stars whose individual masses greatly exceed the accepted 150 Msun stellar mass limit. MNRAS 408, 731
rows.notes: 265 Msun and nearly 9 million suns: right at its Eddington limit (later estimates are somewhat lower)
